claim: Replay priority is need x gain, summed over a belief distribution over future goals (not only the current goal); a goal-general map (one shortest-path Q page per candidate goal, the Geodesic Representation) lets one backup update all goals.
agent_test: Memory store keeps routes for top-k likely future goals ranked by P(goal) x gain; compare with a current-goal-only store at equal tokens on multi-goal tasks.

claim: In a stylised T-maze, a value-replay agent replays only the route to the nearest reward while the map agent replays routes to all goals in order of distance (simulation only, no statistics).
agent_test: Toy planner task with two reachable goals; count tasks solved after a goal switch with route-per-goal memory vs single-goal memory.

claim: Map-replay theory reproduces two rodent datasets where replay lags or opposes behaviour (Gillespie 2021: previous goal arm about 20% of pre-choice remote replay, about 2-fold rate; Carey 2019: choice follows deprivation, replay favours the other arm) using a slow goal-distribution estimate; the fit is qualitative with an assumed learning rate.
agent_test: Give the agent a slow-updating goal prior separate from its fast current-goal belief; test recovery after goal switches.

claim: Gillespie et al. (4 rats, 24/32/23/33 sessions) found remote replay in 34.5-47.2% of SWRs, enriched for the previous goal arm and not for the upcoming choice; replay could not separate correct from error trials. Authors read this as memory maintenance; Sagiv et al. reinterpret it as map prioritisation. The paper also reports a small increase for the future arm.
agent_test: None directly (animal data); use as boundary: do not assume memory access tracks the current plan.

claim: Carey et al.: food/water-deprived rats chose the deprived outcome (89% and 80%) while replay content favoured the other arm; N=4, no independent replication found; final version only seen at abstract level in one line.
agent_test: None directly.

claim: Value-driven replay (reverse replay rises with reward size) is supported by Ambrose 2016 and explained by Mattar and Daw 2018; Pfeiffer and Foster 2013 shows goal-directed forward replay when the goal is stable (Home well). Value replay wins when one goal dominates.
agent_test: Replay current-goal routes first when one goal dominates (cheap default); map replay when goals vary.
audit_note: Ambrose 2016 (only reverse replay rate follows reward change), Mattar & Daw 2018 (explains it via gain term), Pfeiffer & Foster 2013 (forward sequences to HOME well) and Sagiv et al. (value model is special case when a single goal dominates) all consistent; Sagiv quote is about the model reducing to Mattar and Daw, not an empirical 'wins' test.

claim: Goal-general replay is most useful when experience or replay is limited and goals recur or switch (Sagiv et al.). A hindsight-relabeling LLM paper (HSL) is loosely consistent: its WebShop gain is smaller (63.81 to 66.97), which the authors say is 'likely' because WebShop allows only one achievable goal per trajectory, vs ALFWorld unseen 78.36 to 97.76.
agent_test: Run goal-diverse vs single-goal task sets; expect route-per-goal memory to help only on the diverse set.
audit_note: Sagiv et al. says prioritized replay matters in data/compute-limited regimes and reduces to the value model when one goal predominates, but does not say goal-general replay pays off 'only' then; the HSL numbers (WebShop 63.81->66.97, ALFWorld unseen 78.36->97.76) are right, but the single-goal explanation is that paper's hedged 'likely', and the 'same boundary' analogy is the notes' own inference from one preprint.
claim_before_audit: Goal-general replay pays off only when experience or replay is limited and goals recur or switch. LLM relabeling shows the same boundary: smaller gains where a single goal is achievable (WebShop 63.81 to 66.97 vs ALFWorld unseen 78.36 to 97.76).

claim: Hindsight relabeling for LLM agents (HSL, AgentHER, ECHO, SAC-GLAM) reuses a trajectory as a demonstration for other achieved goals: HSL ALFWorld unseen 78.36 to 97.76 (SFT vs SFT+HSL, 1B agent), AgentHER +7.6 to +11.4 pp over SFT-Success (current version; v1 said 7.1-11.7), ECHO up to 80% over a ReAct baseline in average reward. HSL, AgentHER and SAC-GLAM are training-time; ECHO is in-context (prompt-only, no weight updates) and 34 of 40 imputed workflows (85%) reached their goal. All are self-reported; no independent replication of HSL or AgentHER was found.
agent_test: In-context version: after each episode, store the trajectory tagged with every goal it achieved; test reuse on later different goals at equal tokens.
audit_note: Numbers verified (HSL 78.36->97.76 Llama-3.2-1B; AgentHER current abstract +7.6-11.4, v1 +7.1-11.7; ECHO up to 80% over ReAct in XMiniGrid avg reward, 34/40=85%), but 'All are training-time' contradicts the next sentence: ECHO is prompt-only with no weight updates.
claim_before_audit: Hindsight relabeling for LLM agents (HSL, AgentHER, ECHO, SAC-GLAM) improves performance by reusing a trajectory as a demonstration for other achieved goals: HSL ALFWorld unseen 78.36 to 97.76 (SFT vs SFT+HSL, 1B agent), AgentHER +7.6 to +11.4 pp over SFT-Success (current version; v1 said 7.1-11.7), ECHO up to 80% over a ReAct baseline. All are training-time and self-reported. ECHO is in-context (prompt-only, frozen model) and 34 of 40 imputed workflows (85%) reached their goal; HSL and AgentHER have no independent replication found.

claim: Hindsight relabeling needs quality gating: AgentHER label precision 94.1% with one judge vs 97.1% (current version; 97.7% in v1) with multi-judge verification; filtered-out pairs were still 38.7% valid; naive random relabeling hurt.
agent_test: Verify a relabeled goal with a second check before storing a route; measure reuse accuracy with and without the check.

claim: No LLM study found weights stored routes or experiences by an estimated probability of future goals. Nearest neighbours: predictability-gated precompute (sleep-time compute, gain rises with query predictability), value-scored eviction (TraceRetain, AMV-L), hindsight relabeling. Absence is weak evidence: Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex were rate limited.
agent_test: Build the first test: priority = P(goal) x gain on stored routes vs recency vs current-goal-only.
audit_note: Neighbours verified (sleep-time compute gain depends on query predictability; TraceRetain is value-scored eviction in frozen-agent memory); the absence claim itself cannot be verified and is already hedged as weak evidence.

claim: LLMs given graph descriptions handle local edges but fail on multi-step routes in community graphs: GPT-4 succeeded 0 of 30 runs on shortest path one cluster away (max 10% at other temperatures); table means 1-step 0.99, 3-step 0.55, detour 0.55, policy revaluation 0.21; CoT/BFS prompts help only marginally.
agent_test: Check the agent's stored route table against ground truth before use; test on community graphs with an explicit stored map.

claim: Cognitive-map chain of thought (build and mark a map, then plan) raises fine-tuned LM planning on unseen mazes (optimal planning 19.0% none vs 76.5% map with backward unmark); needs training, not just a prompt. Few-shot prompting of the same task gave 0-1% for cognitive-map prompts on Llama-3 and GPT-4o (2024), and a 2026 frontier-model maze test found success depends on input format (80-86% adjacency vs 16-34% visual). A prompt-only modular planner (MAP, GPT-4) did improve graph and Tower of Hanoi planning.
agent_test: Prompt-only map-building step before planning on larger mazes.

claim: Preplay of unpursued but accessible tasks is reflected in human behaviour (partial path reuse 62.39%, CI 53.99-69.53, vs 50% chance, p=0.0049; 62.80% in the shortcut experiment) and beats baselines in deep RL; latent learning fails in parametric systems without episodic retrieval (oracle retrieval helps). Sleep-time compute: about 5x less test-time compute at equal accuracy for a single query per context, a further average cost cut up to 2.5x when about 10 queries share the context, and the gain is larger when the query is more predictable from the context.
agent_test: Pre-compute routes to nearby unpursued goals during idle steps vs retrieve at test time; compare at equal tokens.
audit_note: Preplay numbers (62.39%, CI 53.99-69.53, p=0.0049; 62.80%) and Lampinen oracle-retrieval match; but the sleep-time ~5x saving is for a single query per context, and only the extra amortised 2.5x (t=10, cost-weighted) needs several queries sharing the context.
claim_before_audit: Preplay of unpursued but accessible tasks is reflected in human behaviour (partial path reuse 62.39%, CI 53.99-69.53, vs 50% chance, p=0.0049; 62.80% in the shortcut experiment) and beats baselines in deep RL; latent learning fails in LMs without episodic retrieval (oracle retrieval helps). Sleep-time compute: about 5x less test-time compute at equal accuracy, but only when several queries share the context (2.5x cost cut at t=10) and the query is predictable.

claim: Goal-agnostic stored routes and workflows help LLM agents (Agent Workflow Memory +51.1% relative on WebArena; ExpeL transfer HotpotQA to FEVER 63 to 70% over ReAct; HippoRAG +11 R@2 on 2Wiki) but none found weights memories by likelihood of future goals.
agent_test: Add goal-likelihood weighting to workflow memory and compare against the unweighted store.
audit_note: ExpeL HotpotQA->FEVER transfer is ReAct 63 -> ExpeL Transfer 70 (Act 58); the 59.0 -> 64.2 figures are ExpeL+Reflexion on ALFWorld (R0 vs R3). AWM +51.1% relative and HippoRAG +11 R@2 on 2Wiki (59.2->70.7) are right; the 'none weights by future goal likelihood' part is an unverifiable absence claim.
claim_before_audit: Goal-agnostic stored routes and workflows help LLM agents (Agent Workflow Memory +51.1% relative on WebArena; ExpeL transfer HotpotQA to FEVER 59.0 to 64.2%; HippoRAG +11 R@2 on 2Wiki) but none weights memories by likelihood of future goals.

claim: Rival accounts explain lagging or paradoxical replay without a goal map: memory maintenance, representation protection (r=0.53 single-cell, 0.49 ensemble between separation and paradoxical replay), and experience-strength replay with inhibition of return. A third family appears: adaptation-based local trapping at the current goal (Mallory 2026; replay events at the goal about 2x, shorter, slower).
agent_test: None; note competing explanations.

claim: Bottleneck-state concentration of replay and goal-switching order effects (p11=0.5 vs 0.05) are model predictions not yet tested in animals. Newest dataset checked (Mallory 2026, 4 rats, 44 sessions) keeps the goal fixed within a session, so it cannot test the switching-order prediction and reports no bottleneck analysis.
agent_test: Test whether stored routes through hub/bottleneck steps give more reuse than random routes.

claim: Replay-based updating can repair transition (detour) changes that plain successor representations miss, provided enough offline replay (Russek et al. 2017); humans revalue more after a reward change than after a transition change (Momennejad et al. 2017, N=58, t(57)=2.89, p<0.01).
agent_test: After an environment change, replay hub transitions rather than relearning full values.
audit_note: Russek et al.: SR-Dyna solves the detour task only with enough offline replay (else it degrades to SR-TD); Momennejad et al. bioRxiv Exp 1 N=58 and reward > transition revaluation (t(57)=2.89), but the means 0.52 and 0.45 appear nowhere in the text/legends (possibly only in Fig 4A), so they could not be confirmed; Piray & Daw not opened.
claim_before_audit: Replay-based updating repairs transition (detour) changes that plain successor representations miss; humans revalue after a reward change (0.52) more than after a transition change (0.45), N=58.

claim: Prioritised replay by TD error beats uniform replay on 41 of 49 Atari games; HER with 'future' goal sampling (k=4 or 8) works best among goal-sampling strategies. These are the engineering anchors for value-priority and goal-relabeled replay.
agent_test: Use as reference points for priority and goal-sampling ablations.
audit_note: PER beats uniform replay on 41 of 49 Atari games (abstract); HER paper text says 'future' with k=4 or 8 performs best among strategies.

claim: Preplay for unpursued goals pays back only when stored work is reused: sleep-time compute gain rises with how predictable the next query is, is unfavourable with 1-2 queries per context, favourable with 5-10, and reverses at high test-time budgets.
agent_test: Gate precompute of routes by predicted reuse; compare at equal total tokens across 1, 3, 10 later queries.

claim: In-context hindsight relabeling helps a prompted frozen agent (ECHO: +80% over ReAct on XMiniGrid-Stateful, 42% over next baseline), but accuracy on PeopleJoinQA was 4.6% below Reflexion; label noise is only roughly measured (2 of 40 infeasible imputed workflows) and no noise sweep exists.
agent_test: After each episode tag the trajectory with other achieved goals, verify by replay, then inject noise (0, 10, 25, 50% wrong labels) to find the break point.

claim: Stacked memory types can conflict: fact memory plus reflection cut the discovery-skip rate from 77% to 20% and pass@5 from 58.8% to 52.9% (WikiSQL, 51 examples) compared with either alone; keep one authoritative route per goal.
agent_test: Compare one route per goal against route plus reflection notes at equal tokens.

claim: Bounded-memory eviction does not matter on a clean saturated stream (all policies within Wilson 95% CI on ALFWorld with gpt-5-mini) but does under 75% distractor writes (Precision@5: unbounded 20.2 to 12.4%, FIFO 15.8 to 3.8%, value-scored 16.9 to 16.6%). No test under goal drift exists.
agent_test: Eviction test under goal drift: score = P(goal) x gain x success vs LRU vs LFU, with a mid-run goal-set change.

claim: Rival neural account: Mallory, Widloski and Foster (2026, 4 rats, 44 sessions) find replay at a fixed rewarded goal about twice as frequent, slower and ending at the goal, explained by weaker adaptation, not a goal-general map; the design cannot test goal switching.
agent_test: None directly; use as a reason to keep current-goal routes as well as map routes.
